title: Object designer: a lookup field's "Relationship name" control writes `relationshipName`, a key the spec's FieldSchema does not declare, so the field shows "Unrecognized key" and its save is refused (422)
body:
Filing gate ①: a user-visible authoring defect that contradicts the declared contract. **reach:** a public entry, the console's object designer on a lookup field, measured in Chromium against a live backend and over REST.

**Reader who acts:** objectui triage. The landing is `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectFieldInspector.tsx` (the `InspectorTextField` labelled `designer.field.relationshipName`, lines 1097–1101 on `main` `1d86919`, which commits `patchDef({ relationshipName: v || undefined })`), with its two keys in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`. Filed by `domain:ui` seat 3 (`session_01Vk15bz8xHtKGUfXfCm16h4`) from the os-dev report on objectui#12681 (PR #12752). That PR does not change this. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens
On a lookup field, typing into **Relationship name** (hint: "Inverse collection key on the parent") puts the field in the spec banner, "Fields → job: Unrecognized key(s) on this field: `relationshipName`". The autosave is refused and the field stays Unsaved. The author has no way to save the value the control asks for. Clearing the control does not help either, because the clear patches `relationshipName: undefined` and the key stays on the draft.

## Measured
- Backend: objectstack `66d456d01` `examples/app-crm`, `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh`. The console was objectui `claude/issue-12681-formula-key-omitted` on Vite; that branch does not touch this control. Chromium, real keystrokes.
- A writable package `com.qa.vrf` (namespace `qavrf`), an object `qavrf_job`, and an object `qavrf_rel` with a lookup field `job` → `qavrf_job`.
- Typing `jobs` into Relationship name on `qavrf_rel.job` → the banner above about 1 s later, then the autosave refused.
- REST, the same object body:
  - `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qavrf_rel?package=com.qa.vrf` with `relationshipName: "jobs"` on `fields.job` → **422** `INVALID_METADATA`, `unrecognized_keys` at `fields.job`;
  - without that key → **200**.
- The client probe with the installed `@objectstack/spec` 18.0.0-next.2 `ObjectSchema`: an own `relationshipName` key (with a value, or own-`undefined`) is reported as `unrecognized_keys`.

## The contract (read from source)
- objectstack `packages/spec/src` at `34b740f2d` has no `relationshipName` anywhere. `git log -S relationshipName -- packages/spec/src` finds no commit, so the key was never declared.
- No runtime reads it as a field key. objectstack's only hits are `service-analytics` parameters named `relationshipName` that carry a field NAME, not this key. In objectui the inspector and its two i18n strings are the only non-test hits.
- So the control writes a key that the server refuses and nothing would read.

## Expected
**Governing text:** the skill's ruling principle, "spec 声明 > 实现 > 文档面": where spec and code disagree, the code aligns with the spec. Changing the protocol is a separate card, never an option on a defect card.
- The designer offers no control that writes an undeclared field key. Here that means the Relationship name control and its two i18n keys come out.
- A pin keeps the lookup inspector from writing `relationshipName`.
- Declaring an inverse-collection key in `FieldSchema` would be a separate spec-lane card, with its own business pull.

**Dedupe** (open and closed):
- every objectui `domain:ui` card, 2433 rows, grepped for `relationshipName|relationship name`: 0;
- every objectstack `domain:spec` card, 1776 rows, the same grep: 0;
- the newest 200 issues of each repository, all labels (215 rows after PRs were dropped), the same grep: 0;
- positive controls on the same lists: `setup` 111 hits on objectui, `FieldSchema` 56 on objectstack.

Dedupe words: relationshipName, Relationship name lookup inspector, unrecognized_keys relationshipName, lookup relationship name 422, inverse collection key.
